segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You then, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and what you heard from me before many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be competent to teach others as well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Take your share of hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in the business of everyday life; his aim is to please the one who enlisted him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Likewise, if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes by the rules.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The farmer who does the hard work ought to be the first to share in the crops.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Think over what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my good news,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for which I suffer hardship, even to the point of chains, like a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this reason I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The saying is trustworthy: For if we died with him, we will also live with him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he too will deny us;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: if we are faithless, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Keep reminding people of these things, solemnly charging them before the Lord not to fight over words, which is useful for nothing and ruins those who listen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Make every effort to present yourself to God as one who has passed the test, a worker with no cause for shame, guiding the word of truth along a straight path.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But keep away from profane, empty talk, for those who engage in it will advance further into ungodliness,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and their word will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who have strayed from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The Lord knows those who are his,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from wrongdoing.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for honorable use and some for dishonorable.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So if anyone cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel for honorable use, made holy, useful to the master, prepared for every good work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Flee the desires of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Have nothing to do with foolish and uninstructed disputes, knowing that they breed fights.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a slave of the Lord must not fight, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, patient when wronged,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: instructing opponents with gentleness, in the hope that God may grant them a turning back that leads to knowledge of the truth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and that they may come to their senses and escape the devil’s snare, having been captured alive by him to do his will.

notes.traditional: in the presence of many witnesses / among many witnesses
notes.note: The Greek is literally "through many witnesses." Most translators take it as an idiom for "with many witnesses present," perhaps recalling a public occasion such as Timothy's commissioning. It could instead mean that the teaching was confirmed by, or passed on through, many witnesses.

"Gospel" has become a religious term or a book title. The Greek was an ordinary word for the announcement of good news, used also of public and imperial proclamations. Many modern translations alternate between the two renderings.

This translation normally renders this adjective "faithful," as in verses 2 and 13. Applied to a saying, "faithful" is unnatural in modern English, so "trustworthy" is used, as in most recent translations. The formula recurs in the letters to Timothy and Titus. The lines that follow, through verse 13, are widely thought to quote an early hymn or confession.

The verb can mean "fail to believe" or "prove unfaithful." The play on "he remains faithful" favours the second, and the rendering keeps that echo. It is also debated whether this line is a comfort (his faithfulness outlasts our failure) or a warning (he stays true to his word, including the warning of verse 12).

Manuscripts are divided here between "before the Lord" and "before God." The SBLGNT text translated here reads "the Lord"; other critical editions and translations based on them read "God." The sense is hardly affected.

notes.phrase: guiding the word of truth along a straight path
notes.traditional: rightly dividing the word of truth / rightly handling the word of truth
notes.note: The verb is rare. Its only earlier known uses are in the Greek version of Proverbs (3:6; 11:5), where it means to cut or make a road straight. The rendering follows that usage: the message is to be kept on a straight course, in contrast to the teachers of verses 16–18 who have strayed. Most modern translations paraphrase as "correctly handling"; the older "rightly dividing" rests on the word's parts, not on its attested use.

notes.phrase: the resurrection has already taken place
notes.note: These teachers apparently held that resurrection was a purely spiritual event already experienced by believers, perhaps at conversion or baptism, leaving no future bodily resurrection to hope for. The details of their teaching are not known. Paul treats it as striking at the centre of the faith (compare 1 Corinthians 15).

A seal was an inscription or stamp marking ownership and authenticity. The first inscription quotes Numbers 16:5 in its Greek form, from the story of Korah's rebellion against Moses. The second is not an exact quotation of any one passage but echoes scriptural language, possibly including the same story (Numbers 16:26) and Isaiah 26:13.

notes.traditional: from these / from what is dishonorable
notes.note: "These" most naturally refers to the dishonorable vessels of verse 20, that is, the false teachers and their influence. It could also refer more loosely to the errors and wrongdoing just described. Some translations make the second reading explicit.

The Greek word denotes a slave, someone owned by a master, not a hired servant. "Servant" is traditional and softens this. The phrase also echoes the Old Testament title "servant of the Lord," given to Moses, David and the prophets, which the Greek Scriptures often render with this word; there it is a title of honour as well as of ownership.
"Meekness" now suggests weakness or timidity, which the Greek does not. The word describes a gentle, unassertive manner. "Gentleness" is the usual rendering in modern translations.

"Repentance" now centres on feeling sorry. The Greek word, shaped by the prophets' call to "return" to God, describes a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep "repentance" as an established term understood to include a change of life.

notes.phrase: by him to do his will
notes.traditional: taken captive by him at his will / captured by him to do his will
notes.note: The Greek uses two different pronouns, and it is disputed whom each refers to. The rendering follows the majority view that both refer to the devil. Alternatively, the opponents escape the devil who captured them in order to do God's will, or they are "captured alive" by the Lord's slave to do God's will.

candidates.reason: Recurs across the whole New Testament, and translations split between "slave," "servant" and "bondservant," especially in the phrase "slave of the Lord/Christ."
"The elect" is traditional and theologically loaded, while "the chosen" is plainer; the choice should be uniform across the Gospels, Paul, 1 Peter and Revelation.
"Sanctify," "make holy," "set apart" and "consecrate" all appear in translations, and the word-family (ἅγιος, ἁγιασμός) needs one coordinated decision.
Rendered variously as "lusts," "passions" and "desires"; "lust" now narrows the meaning to sexual desire, which misleads in many passages.
The verb and its noun ὑπομονή are rendered "endure," "persevere," "patience" and "steadfastness" across books, obscuring a key recurring theme.

patch.reason: euangelion promoted to active after full-run drift (good news 37 / gospel 35)
